title: Tributary shadow fanout with credit-aware throttle and tenant isolation
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Goal: implement a safe, tenant-aware shadow/mirroring pipeline ("tributary" pattern) that allows non-blocking traffic duplication to candidate model variants while enforcing per-tenant credit budgets, strong isolation, and cost governance. The feature should enable continuous evaluation and offline metrics collection without exposing production customers to risk or unexpected billing.

Background: current shadowing approaches are either all-or-nothing or rely on coarse sampling which does not scale across hundreds/thousands of tenants with varied budgets. We need a mechanism that treats mirrored traffic as a first-class, metered consumer: tenants can opt-in or be included for internal experiments, the platform can cap mirrored cost per tenant, and the system enforces safety gates if mirrored load causes regressions.

Scope: build an ingress-level fanout that duplicates requests into one or more mirror lanes, implements credit-token-based throttles per-tenant and per-environment, persists mirrored payloads where needed for offline evals, and exposes observability and chargeback metrics. Include runtime kill-switches and an automated rollback signaler that interacts with rollouts (canaries/A-B) when mirror-driven regressions are detected.
acceptance_criteria: Mirror fanout implemented in ingress path as non-blocking duplication with <1ms median added tail latency under typical load (measured on staging)
Per-tenant mirror credits enforced: each tenant has configurable mirrored token budget and once exhausted mirrored requests are dropped or sampled according to policy
Mirror lane failures do not impact primary request success path (end-to-end request success rate unchanged)
Observability: per-tenant mirrored_qps, mirror_drop_rate, mirror_cost_estimate and mirrored_error_rate surfaced in Console and usable for alerting

Automated rollback trigger: if mirrored_error_rate for candidate model exceeds baseline by >2% absolute or candidate latency P95 increases by >25% over baseline for 3 consecutive minutes, the system flags the rollout and posts an alert to the rollout controller
Data handling: mirrored payloads are redacted via the platform PII rules, encrypted in transit and at rest, and retained only for the configured TTL
E2E tests and a staging run across representative tenant sizes completed before merging
tasks: Implement non-blocking fanout at ingress (sidecar and gateway paths)
Add per-tenant credit/token bucket store (Redis-backed) and admin API
Implement dynamic sampling policy when credits exhausted (configurable: drop, reservoir-sample, best-effort low-fidelity capture)
Integrate mirror lane telemetry with Console (per-tenant metrics and dashboards)
Add security redaction/encryption hooks for mirrored payloads
Create automated rollback signal generator and integrate with rollout controller
Write e2e tests and run staged rollout against internal tenants
testing_plan: Unit tests for credit bucket logic and sampling behavior
Load tests: ramp mirrored QPS to 5x normal for small/medium/large tenants and measure primary path latency and error budget impact
Chaos tests: introduce transient mirror lane failures and confirm primary requests remain unaffected
Smoke staging rollout: enable tributary mirroring for 5 internal tenants, validate metrics and automated signals
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): local run + integration tests (PRs) - team only
Phase 1 (internal): enable for ops and internal test tenants with generous credits; run for 48h and validate stability
Phase 2 (select customers): opt-in cohort of 10 low-risk tenants with tight credit budgets; monitor for 7 days
Phase 3 (wider): enable default sampling for small tenants and low sampling for larger tenants with chargeback enabled

Rollback criteria: mirrored_error_rate delta >2% absolute OR candidate latency P95 increase >25% sustained for 3 minutes OR mirror_cost_estimate burn rate >150% of configured budget across top-10 tenants -> trigger automated rollback and paging
decisions: Use ingress-level fanout instead of sidecar-only to support both hosted and private modes with a single control surface
Credit token store: choose Redis for low-latency global counters with periodic persisted snapshots for accounting
Default policy when credits exhausted: reservoir sampling with probabilistic retention to keep evaluation signal while bounding cost
Mirror payloads will be stored in a separate, encrypted tenant-scoped bucket with configurable TTL (default 7 days)
risks: Cost overruns if credit accounting has edge-case races - mitigate with conservative defaults and safety margins
Increased primary request latency during extreme load if fanout backpressure is mishandled - mitigate with non-blocking async pipelines and circuit breakers
Data exposure risk from mirrored payloads - mitigate with enforced redaction, encryption, and short TTLs
Operational complexity for private deployments with air-gapped networks - provide a trimmed mode that skips persistent capture and only forwards metrics
